subject: POC environment plan & success criteria — Juno Health pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@junohealth.com>, Matthew Lee <matthew.lee@junohealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: POC environment plan & success criteria — Juno Health pilot

Hi Samira / Matt —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have aligned expectations for the pilot. I captured what I heard on the call (success criteria, constraints, and an initial environment recommendation). Please review and flag anything I missed.

High-level ask from Juno on the call:
- Validate Redwood’s ability to serve note-generation and medical-coding suggestions against a 12M-token monthly workload with 95th percentile latency < 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Verify privacy controls: data residency (US), customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for all inference requests.
- Confirm costs and an ops plan for a 6-week POC with production-like throughput.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
1) Latency: 95th p95 of generation requests for 128-token prompts <= 300ms over a 48-hour sustained run at target throughput.
2) Throughput: sustain 300 concurrent sessions (avg 1.2 req/s per session) for 48 hours without error rate > 1%.
3) Quality: model produces acceptable coding suggestions per your internal evaluation (>= 85% pass on the sample prompt set — see attached spreadsheet).
4) Security: KMS integration test and end-to-end audit logs present in the Redshift export for at least 30 days.
5) Operational handoff: Redwood runbook with escalation and run-rate cost estimate delivered at POC close.

Environment recommendation (initial):
- We recommend a VPC Trial (private control plane) for this POC. Reasoning: your need for customer-managed KMS + auditability + US-only egress strongly favors VPC. A VPC trial gives us the ability to replicate the production networking constraints and validates deployment automation.
- Contingency / fast path: if procurement timeline prevents VPC before the kickoff, we can run an isolated Dedicated Sandbox in our hosted region with strict data handling rules for a short interim (we'll document differences in expected telemetry).

Immediate next steps (owner):
- Juno: confirm the 3 sample prompt sets and provide a list of 10 representative coding prompts (Samira) — due Wed 2027-06-09.
- Redwood (Olga): send success-criteria workbook and VPC checklist (attached) and proposed kickoff agenda — sent.
- Redwood (Vivek): scope network/VPC prerequisites and estimate time-to-standup (ETA in separate email).

Attachments: juno-poc-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet with example prompts & pass/fail cols), redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (network & IAM checklist).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 18:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC environment plan & success criteria — Juno Health pilot

Thanks Olga — adding a few technical clarifications for Samira & Matt so procurement/infra can prep.

Short summary: VPC trial works and will validate all controls you requested. Key infra items that will impact timeline:
- Customer KMS: we need an IAM role in your account with Put/Get permissions scoped to a dedicated key (we can provide a CloudFormation snippet). Plan for 2 business days to validate once creds available.
- Network egress: ensure NAT/egress rules allow outbound to our control-plane endpoints (I list domains in the checklist). If your VPC has restrictive NACLs, we may need a short window with relaxed rules for initial validation.
- Storage for audit logs: we can ship to your S3 (preferred) or pull via connector — S3 will be faster to validate retention.
- Test harness: for the 48-hour throughput run we'll provide a lightweight load generator container (Docker image + k6 script) and a runbook.

ETA: assuming we get KMS keys + basic VPC peering info by Thu 6/10, engineering can spin up the trial environment in ~8 business days (standup + smoke tests). If timeline must be compressed to 3 business days, we recommend Dedicated Sandbox path (hosted) and a short controlled dataset to avoid exposing production credentials.

Quick risk note: if model quantization is required to hit cost targets, we should lock the model variant before the run; quantization can affect subtle output differences — we'll include a regression eval step in the QA checklist.

I'll attach the CloudFormation snippet and NAT egress domains in a follow-up.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Inference Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Samira — great questions. Quick answers and an adjusted proposal to keep momentum while procurement finalizes the KMS.

1) Minimal unblock path (before KMS available): we can run a limited-hosted Dedicated Sandbox with anonymized payloads and encrypted-at-rest using Redwood-managed keys. This allows you to validate latency/throughput and the QA pipeline. Differences vs VPC:
   - KMS: Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys (we'll provide a clear statement and SOC2 controls). VPC uses your customer-managed KMS with direct key access.
   - Network isolation: Hosted is isolated per-customer but not in your VPC — we simulate IP whitelisting and strict routing.
   - Audit pipeline: hosted sandbox can stream anonymized audit logs to a test S3 bucket we control; we'll provide the log format and a sample export for legal review.

2) Next steps and owners / timeline (updated):
- Today (Olga): attach hosted-vs-vpc short comparison doc; schedule kickoff for 6/15 (tentative).
- 2027-06-09 (Samira): share 10 representative prompts (confirmed).
- 2027-06-10 (Vivek): share CloudFormation snippet + egress domains and a rough ETA for VPC standup (8 business days estimate).
- 2027-06-21 (Juno procurement): provide KMS key (if available) — otherwise continue hosted-sandbox validation.
- 2027-06-22 to 2027-07-06: run POC (6-week window) — final dates to be confirmed at kickoff.

I've attached a short Hosted vs VPC comparison and the success-criteria workbook to this mail for your review. If you're OK, I'll lock the kickoff for Tue 2027-06-15 at 16:00 PT and send an invite (we'll use that meeting to finalize the test plan and the runbook owners).

Attachments: juno-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf, hosted-vs-vpc-comparison.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
